subject: StellarBank: private cluster deployment — node/storage/network playbook
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@stellarbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: StellarBank: private cluster deployment — node/storage/network playbook

Hi Rajiv,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our conversation, I put together a concise playbook that captures recommended cluster sizing, node pool separation, and storage topology for the on-prem private deployment. This is intended to align with your compliance needs (KMS-backed encryption, audit forwarding) and your desire for a predictable inference SLO (95th p50 token latency targets). Attached: a SKU matrix and a topology sketch.

Executive summary (short):
- Two control-plane replicas (HA) running on dedicated mgmt nodes; etcd backed by RAID1 local NVMe for performance and durability.
- Three node-pool classes: 
  - inference-gpu: GPU nodes (A100/ H100 eq.) with 512GB+ NVMe for model cache + 1 TB ephemeral NVMe for temp KV cache. Taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule.
  - inference-cpu: high-cpu instances (48–96 vCPU, 384GB RAM) for batching workers and multi-tenant routing.
  - infra/system: small nodes for logging/monitoring/ingress, and a separate storage-proxy pool for CSI/rook pods.
- Storage pattern: 
  - Ephemeral local NVMe for token-level KV cache and model shards (fastest path).
  - Durable shared storage for artifacts and checkpoints: enterprise NFS backed by SAN or Ceph RBD with encryption at rest; use topology-aware PV provisioning (zone/hostname).
  - Avoid using Rook on the same disks as inference workloads; dedicate separate disks or use external Ceph cluster managed by ops.
- Networking: dual-NIC recommendation (mgmt + dataplane), VLAN segmentation for control/tenant/e2e egress, and strict ACLs that block outbound to public unless routed through approved NAT gateway. BGP advertised egress for low-latency multi-site failover.
- Security/compliance: KMS/HSM integration for envelope encryption; audit log forwarders to your SIEM (syslog over TLS).

Risks & mitigations:
- Local SSD eviction during full disks -> enforce kubelet eviction thresholds (imagefs.available, nodefs.available) and monitor disk pressure alerts.
- CSI driver latency on small nodes -> run CSI drivers on dedicated infra pool and enable async provisioning.
- Model drift/regression after quantization -> pin model versions in Redwood and run rollout canaries with 5% traffic.

Next steps / asks from StellarBank ops team:
1) Confirm allowed GPU SKUs and max per-rack power draw (so we can finalize node count).
2) Confirm SAN vs Ceph preference and whether you want Redwood to operate Ceph or connect to existing storage.
3) Provide the IP ranges for management VLAN and egress NAT.

I captured these as two attachments (SKU matrix + topology PNG). If you want, Grace and I can join a 30-minute MOP session to walk infra through the plan.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Kimberly—

Appreciate the crisp summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock SKU/quantities: 
1) For the inference-gpu pool, do you expect the model shard cache to be replicated across nodes or reconstructed on cold-start? What is the recommended warmup strategy for 2–3 TB models?
2) On the shared storage side: we currently have a NetApp SAN (iSCSI) and a small Ceph cluster used by batch workloads. Preference would be to avoid adding an operator-managed Ceph unless we have to. Is NetApp over iSCSI acceptable for persistent volumes with the CSI driver?
3) We need to ensure any data-at-rest keys are controlled by our HSM vendor (Thales). Can Redwood integrate with an external HSM for envelope keys?

Also, we need a short MOP (checklist) for our change control ticket. Could you draft the minimal pre-checks and post-validation steps?

Thanks,
Rajiv Menon
Director, Platform Engineering
StellarBank
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@stellarbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StellarBank: private cluster deployment — node/storage/network playbook

Rajiv—

Great questions, answered inline below. I've attached a short MOP checklist PDF for your change control (signed by Redwood engineering) and a brief warmup plan.

1) Model shard cache: recommended approach is hybrid — keep a replicated hot-cache for the most recent shards (async replication across 2 nodes per rack) and a reconstruction path from durable shared storage for cold starts. For 2–3 TB models we suggest: prefetch the first N token windows to local NVMe on pod init, run a background loader to fetch remaining shards, and use a traffic ramp (10%/30%/100%) over 20 minutes. This keeps tail latency bounded.

2) NetApp SAN over iSCSI: yes, acceptable if you expose it via a supported CSI driver and ensure multipath is enabled on the nodes. Key caveats: ensure PV topology constraints so pods land in the same rack/zone as their backing LUN; avoid heavy small-I/O random writes on the SAN—use local NVMe for write-heavy cache and the SAN for durable checkpoints and model blobs.

3) HSM integration: Redwood supports external KMS/HSM for envelope keys (we have integrations with Vault HSM and several vendors, and can work with Thales for key wrapping). We will need your KMS endpoints and a service account with the ability to perform Encrypt/Decrypt and GenerateDataKey operations.

Attached MOP highlights (high level):
- Pre-change: node health check, disk SMART verification, base image & kernel patch levels, firewall rule staging, test KMS handshake, CSI driver smoke test.
- During change: cordon + drain strategy for inference nodes with priority batching, controlled model cache prefetch, monitor eviction thresholds.
- Post-change: run synthetic inference workload (latency + tail checks), verify audit log forwarding, validate PV mount consistency and failover.

I attached the checklist as: 20261105-signed-mop-checklist.pdf (we initialled the steps we take with you). Grace can schedule the MOP session; Marcus will follow up on multipath configuration details.

Would you like Redwood to operate the Ceph cluster or to integrate with your NetApp? If NetApp is preferred, we will prepare an iSCSI multipath guide and updated storage class manifest.

Best,
Kimberly
